values: 'Original work order deleted after a build: its number shows as plain text

'The spec now says that when the work order the inspection was run on is deleted after a build onto a new work order, the build note and the Audit Log entry show its number as text with no link; the note and Audit Log cases never delete a work order.

'S7-R2: 7 Oct 2026 (Deleted work order after a build)
S7-R5: 7 Oct 2026 (Deleted work order after a build)

'The shop has ShopCoach and at least one labor type.
You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit', 'Work orders - Create & Edit' and 'View History Logs', and you can delete work orders.
A completed inspection with a Not OK finding, on a work order you can delete (for example S1-2252).

'1. Open the completed inspection, press Build lines and choose A new work order.
2. Wait for the proposed lines and press Add Lines.
3. Note the new work order's number (for example S1-2301).
4. Delete the original work order (S1-2252 in the example).
5. Open the new work order's Notes tab and find the note saying the lines were built from the inspection.
6. Open the new work order's Audit Log and find the 'Built from inspection' entry.

'Step 5: the note shows the original work order's number as plain text, tagged 'Work order deleted', with no link.
Step 6: the Audit Log entry shows the original work order's number as plain text, with no link.

'Verdict KEEP, copied as is. The tag appears only on the note, not on the Audit Log entry, exactly as the spec words it. Building onto a new work order needs ShopCoach: run on Staging (SV-11084).
'A kept inspection follows its work order's asset at deletion and on merge

'PRD v43 says a kept inspection uses its stored asset, but the PM's later decision (8 Oct, not yet in the PRD) says it takes the asset the work order has when it is deleted, and merges then move it; no case changes the asset before deleting, merges a kept inspection, or checks its photos survive.

'SV-10960: 8 Oct 2026 (Milos Vasic (PM) in Jira; not yet in PRD v43 ('I'll add this to the PRD'))
S5-R21: 7 Oct 2026 (Deleted work order: outcome, footer, reopened, merge (SV-10965))
S5-E3: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)

'You are signed in with 'Customers - View', 'Work orders - View' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', and you can delete work orders and edit assets.
A customer with three assets: asset A (for example unit 1001), asset B (for example unit 2002) and asset C (for example unit 3003). Asset C has a VIN; write it down.
A work order on asset A with a completed inspection and its report; one answer in it carries a photo.

'1. On the work order, change the asset from asset A to asset B and save.
2. Delete the work order.
3. Open asset B's Inspections tab.
4. Open asset A's Inspections tab.
5. On asset B's tab, open the kept inspection and look at the answer that had a photo.
6. Open asset B, change its VIN to asset C's VIN, save, and answer Yes to 'Would you like to merge with the already existing asset?'.
7. Open asset C's Inspections tab.

'Step 3: the inspection is listed on asset B, the asset the work order had when it was deleted, with a dash in the Work order column.
Step 4: the inspection is not listed on asset A.
Step 5: the inspection opens read-only and the photo is still there.
Step 7: the inspection is listed on asset C, which survives the merge because asset B's VIN was changed to asset C's.
=HYPERLINK("https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/cases/view/88532","C88532")

'Verdict FIX, every correction applied. Divergence to disclose in the case: PRD v43 S5-R21 still reads "When the work order has been deleted, the stored asset is used (S5-E3)"; expected steps 3-4 follow Milos Vasic's later SV-10960 ruling (8 Oct), which he said he would add to the PRD but v43 (13 Oct, an S15-only edit) does not carry. Latest wins, so the case follows the ruling; ask the PM to update S5-R21. Expected step 7 now names the asset that survives the merge. Step 5 follows v43 S5-E3 (a kept inspection is a read-only record; deleting the work order must not delete its photos). Built on sv8181 per SV-10965 (Stefan Vukovic, 8 Oct, steps 8-9); the VIN edit + Yes merge route is documented there.
'Anyone who can open the inspection can open its reference and follow-up files

'The spec changed on 29 Sep: opening a reference file or a follow-up file no longer needs 'Work Orders — View'; anyone who can view the inspection can open them. The file cases are all run by a user who has that permission.

'S11 prerequisites: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered (Milos Vasic, PM: 'Reference files open for anyone who can view the inspection.'))
S19 prerequisites: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered (Milos Vasic, PM))

Step 5: the follow-up file opens in the viewer, although the user does not have 'Work orders - View'.

'Verdict FIX, correction applied: the earlier role example ('a technician role with Work Order Lines - Create & Edit only') was an assumption, not a source fact, and is removed. Before this test ships, prove on the build that a user without 'Work orders - View' can reach and open an inspection at all (inspections are opened from a work order's line; the spec names no route that avoids viewing the work order). If no such user can open an inspection, the precondition is unreachable and the change has nothing a tester can observe: drop the test and tell the QA lead. Answering Not OK without submitting is fine even with the default note rule on. File names are links, with no separate Open or View button.
'Long names end with '…' and show the full name on hover

'The designer decided on 12 Oct that long names are cut with '…' and show the full name on hover; the updated builder case covers only the builder, so the fill screen, the work order row, Start Inspection, the completed screen and the asset tab are not checked.
'SV-11103: 12 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic (designer) in Jira)

'Verdict KEEP, copied as is; only the combined expected line 'Steps 2, 4, 6 and 8' was split into one line per step so each starts 'Step N:' (no content change).
